note: Three hand-authored personas for the Dietetic Assessment composite engine (MUST + GLIM + NRS-2002 + SARC-F + SCOFF + NICE CG32 refeeding risk, max-grade composite). Verified: unlike several sibling engines in this backlog, the MUST scorers (scoreMustBmi/scoreMustWeightLoss) push a fired rule for EVERY branch, including a genuine score of 0 (R-MUST-BMI-0, R-MUST-WL-0) - there is no null/zero-means-silent convention here. GLIM diagnosis requires at least one phenotypic AND at least one etiologic criterion; if either list is empty the diagnosis is 'none' regardless of how severe the populated list is. computeBmi returns bmi:null (not an estimated numeric value) whenever weight is missing, which cascades: the MUAC fallback still scores MUST, but every later bmi-gated check (GLIM low-bmi, refeeding bmi<14/16/18.5, R-COMPOSITE-BMI-16, F-SEVERE-UNDERWEIGHT-001) is silently skipped rather than estimated. scoreRefeedingRisk returns as soon as it finds 'highest' risk (bmi<14 or >15 days negligible intake) WITHOUT evaluating the major/minor criteria at all, so a highest-risk patient never accumulates the high-risk major/minor rule rows even if several would independently qualify - only the 'highest' rule fires. Regenerate expected with: bin/test-personas dietic-assessment --update

personas.name: Well-nourished routine review - MUST 0, no findings
personas.description: BMI 22.0 (usual weight equals current weight, so 0% loss), not acutely ill, oral intake 95% of usual. Expect mustScore 0 ('low'), bmi 22, glimDiagnosis 'none', refeedingRisk 'none', computedCompositeRisk and finalCompositeRisk both 'low', recommendation 'routine-care', two fired rules (R-MUST-BMI-0, R-MUST-WL-0 - both genuine zero-score audit rows, not omitted), and no flags.

firedRules.description: Body mass index 22 kg/m² is above 20.0.
Unplanned weight loss of 0% against usual weight is below 5%.

personas.name: Declined weighing - MUAC fallback, subjective weight loss, isolated GLIM diagnosis
personas.description: Non-critical edge case: the patient declined weighing, so height/weight are both blank and mid-upper-arm circumference (21 cm, between 20 and 23.5) drives the MUST BMI score via the MUAC fallback (R-MUST-MUAC-1) rather than a computed bmi - bmi itself stays null throughout the whole result, not an estimated number. No baseline weight exists, so the subjective MUST criterion applies instead (clothes/jewellery looser -> R-MUST-WL-SUBJECTIVE). Moderate muscle wasting at 2 of 3 sites satisfies the GLIM reduced-muscle-mass phenotypic criterion (moderate severity), and oral intake at 45% of usual (at or below the 50% GLIM threshold) satisfies the reduced-intake etiologic criterion - both lists are non-empty, so glimDiagnosis is 'moderate' (R-GLIM-DX). Expect mustScore 2 ('high', from BMI 1 + weight-loss 1), bmi null, refeedingRisk 'none' (every refeeding threshold is bmi- or weight-loss-percent-gated and both are null here), computedCompositeRisk and finalCompositeRisk both 'high', recommendation 'dietetic-treatment-plan', six fired rules (R-MUST-MUAC-1, R-MUST-WL-SUBJECTIVE, R-GLIM-P-MM, R-GLIM-E-INTAKE, R-GLIM-DX, R-COMPOSITE-INTAKE), and two flags: F-HIGH-MALNUTRITION-RISK-001, F-INADEQUATE-ORAL-INTAKE-001 (both high).

firedRules.description: Mid-upper-arm circumference 21 cm is below 23.5, suggesting a body mass index below 20.0.
No baseline weight available; clothes or jewellery reported as looser, so the MUST subjective criterion is applied.
Moderate muscle wasting on physical examination (2 of 3 sites affected).
Oral intake is 45% of usual, at or below the GLIM 50% threshold.
GLIM moderate malnutrition: 1 phenotypic and 1 etiologic criteria met.
Oral intake is 45% of usual, below half of the estimated requirement.

flags.description: MUST score 2 places the patient in the high-risk category.
flags.suggestedAction: Treat: agree a dietetic care plan, improve and increase overall nutritional intake, and monitor against it.

flags.description: Oral intake is 45% of usual, below half of the estimated requirement.
flags.suggestedAction: Start food-first fortification and consider oral nutritional supplements; review whether an alternative feeding route is needed.

personas.name: Critical - refeeding-highest risk with an unsafe swallow and fourteen safety flags
personas.description: Critical/highest-severity persona layering nearly every instrument at once: bmi 12.9 (below both the refeeding-highest threshold of 14 and the composite critical threshold of 16), 17.5% unintentional weight loss against the usual weight of 40 kg (exceeds the composite 15% critical threshold), acutely ill with no intake for over 5 days (MUST acute score 2, giving mustScore 6), oral intake at 20% of usual, dysphagia reported with no speech-and-language-therapy assessment AND a failed swallow screen (both dysphagia flags plus the composite unsafe-swallow rule), an NRS-2002 score of 5, a SARC-F score of 10 (maximum, at-risk), a positive SCOFF score of 3, low potassium (3.2, below 3.5), HbA1c 90 (poorly controlled diabetes), eGFR 25 with an oral-nutritional-supplement plan (a renal/high-protein conflict), and a recorded safeguarding concern. Verified quirk: because bmi<14 makes scoreRefeedingRisk return 'highest' immediately, none of the separate major/minor refeeding criteria (several of which - the low potassium, the >15% weight loss, the >10-day negligible intake - would independently qualify) are evaluated or recorded as their own rule rows; only the single R-REFEED-HIGHEST rule fires for refeeding. GLIM diagnosis is 'severe' (both a severe weight-loss and a severe low-bmi phenotypic criterion, plus reduced-intake and inflammation etiologic criteria). Expect mustScore 6 ('high' MUST band), bmi 12.9, glimDiagnosis 'severe', refeedingRisk 'highest', computedCompositeRisk and finalCompositeRisk both 'critical', recommendation 'urgent-referral', sixteen fired rules, and fourteen flags spanning high and medium priority.

firedRules.description: Body mass index 12.9 kg/m² is below 18.5.
Unplanned weight loss of 17.5% against usual weight exceeds 10%.
Acutely ill with no nutritional intake, or unlikely intake, for more than five days.
Unintentional weight loss of 17.5% within 6 months meets the GLIM severe threshold.
Body mass index 12.9 kg/m² is below 20, the GLIM severe threshold for this age band.
Oral intake is 20% of usual, at or below the GLIM 50% threshold.
Acute or chronic disease burden with C-reactive protein 45 mg/L.
GLIM severe malnutrition: 2 phenotypic and 2 etiologic criteria met.
SARC-F score 10 is at or above the at-risk threshold of 4.
SCOFF score 3 is at or above the threshold of 2 for further eating-disorder assessment.
Body mass index 12.9 kg/m² is below 14.
NRS-2002 score 5 is at or above the at-risk threshold of 3.
Oral intake is 20% of usual, below half of the estimated requirement.
Body mass index 12.9 kg/m² is below 16.
Unintentional weight loss of 17.5% exceeds 15%.
An unsafe or unassessed swallow carries an aspiration risk.

flags.description: MUST score 6 places the patient in the high-risk category.
flags.suggestedAction: Treat: agree a dietetic care plan, improve and increase overall nutritional intake, and monitor against it.

flags.description: Body mass index 12.9 kg/m² is below 16.0.
flags.suggestedAction: Assess for refeeding-syndrome risk before starting nutrition support, and involve the nutrition support team.

flags.description: Unintentional weight loss of 17.5% in the last 3 to 6 months.
flags.suggestedAction: Investigate the cause of the weight loss and start nutrition support with refeeding precautions.

flags.description: Highest risk of refeeding syndrome per NICE CG32.
flags.suggestedAction: Check potassium, phosphate, magnesium, and calcium before feeding. Start at 5 kcal/kg/day with cardiac monitoring and specialist nutrition-support-team input.

flags.description: Dysphagia reported with no speech-and-language-therapy assessment recorded.
flags.suggestedAction: Refer to speech and language therapy before agreeing a texture or fluid consistency; withhold oral intake if the swallow is unsafe.
Keep the patient nil by mouth pending a speech-and-language-therapy swallow assessment.

flags.description: Oral intake is 20% of usual, below half of the estimated requirement.
flags.suggestedAction: Start food-first fortification and consider oral nutritional supplements; review whether an alternative feeding route is needed.

flags.description: Little or no nutritional intake for 12 days.
flags.suggestedAction: Escalate to the nutrition support team; assess refeeding risk before starting nutrition support.
Correct before or alongside feeding; a low pre-feeding electrolyte is a refeeding-syndrome high-risk criterion.

flags.description: SCOFF score 3 is at or above the threshold of 2.
flags.suggestedAction: Refer to the eating-disorder service; avoid weight-focused goals and consider not sharing the weight reading.

flags.description: eGFR 25 ml/min with a high-protein or supplemented plan.
flags.suggestedAction: Discuss protein, potassium, and phosphate targets with the renal dietetic team before implementing the plan.
Follow local safeguarding policy and raise a concern with the safeguarding lead the same day.

flags.description: SARC-F score 10 is at or above the at-risk threshold of 4.
flags.suggestedAction: Combine a higher-protein plan with resistance exercise and consider a physiotherapy referral.

flags.description: HbA1c 90 mmol/mol indicates poorly controlled diabetes.
flags.suggestedAction: Coordinate the carbohydrate plan with the diabetes team before increasing energy intake.
